findings.description: REQ-ENTRY-001 (tap time slot opens creation form) and REQ-ENTRY-004 (tap existing entry opens detail view) are mapped to PROP-005 (offline data round-trip) and PROP-010 (calendar rendering positions). Neither proof obligation verifies the tap-to-form navigation behavior. The form-opening UX is untested. In lean mode this is acceptable if covered implicitly by component tests during implementation.

REQ-CAL-006 (color-code entries by category) is mapped to PROP-010 which only describes positional rendering ('correct time slots'). REQ-CHART-007 (chart colors matching calendar) is mapped to PROP-012 which only tests period data correctness. No proof obligation explicitly verifies color consistency between calendar and charts.

EDGE-001 midnight split clarification is well-specified for per-day counting, but the spec does not address what happens in the weekly bar chart: is the entry counted once in the aggregate or split across its constituent days? The daily rule is clear but the weekly aggregation rule for split entries is implicit.

Iteration-1 finding (medium severity) about REQ-API-001 and REQ-API-004 was not addressed. REQ-API-001 (Elysia.js + Expo API routes integration) and REQ-API-004 (TanStack Query + optimistic updates) remain mapped only to PROP-008, which verifies Valibot validation and Result pattern. The Elysia route registration and TanStack Query optimistic update rollback behavior have no dedicated proof obligation. In lean mode this is acceptable as integration smoke coverage, but the gap is documented.

Iteration-1 finding (medium severity) about purity boundary tier contradiction was not addressed. Section 1 lists notifications/scheduler testing strategy as 'Unit tests with expo-notifications mock', but PROP-009 is classified as Tier 2 (Integration). The tier label and the stated strategy are inconsistent. Functionally harmless but creates confusion for implementers.

Sprint decomposition (Section 5) does not reference the new proof obligations PROP-016 through PROP-030. Sprint 4 lists PROP-009 and PROP-013 but not PROP-016/017 (notification flows) or PROP-025/026/027 (category CRUD, reorder, delete confirm). Sprint 5 does not list PROP-018 (data isolation), PROP-019-023 (edge cases), PROP-028-030 (chart empty state, perf benchmarks). Implementers following the sprint plan will miss these obligations.

notAddressed: Purity boundary tier contradiction (downgraded to low)

summary: All critical and high-severity findings from iteration 1 have been resolved. Edge cases EDGE-001 through EDGE-007 now have dedicated proof obligations (PROP-019 to PROP-023). Overloaded PROPs have been split appropriately. Performance NFRs have dedicated benchmarks (PROP-029, PROP-030). Data isolation has its own proof obligation (PROP-018). Sync timestamp ambiguity is resolved with server-assigned HLC. Two medium-severity iteration-1 findings (API integration coverage, purity tier label) were not explicitly addressed but are acceptable in lean mode. The sprint decomposition omits new PROP IDs, which should be corrected before sprint planning. Overall, the spec and verification architecture are now sufficient for implementation.
